title: An intrinsically trained fly model matched an observed future-turn signal
summary: Among 20 intrinsic learning objectives, DIAYN produced virtual fly policies that most closely matched the relationship between neural and behavioral prediction of future turns in prior fruit-fly recordings. The comparison evaluated signals 15 to 8 seconds before a turn. It supports a computational model of the observed behavior.
organization: University of Maryland, College Park; Carnegie Mellon University

source_review.scope: v1 policy comparison, prospective decoding Figure 3 and Results

evidence.tested: The researchers held the digital embodiment and comparison assay consistent while varying intrinsic learning objectives and comparing frozen policies with prior aggregate observations.
evidence.unknown: The behavior and neural comparisons test a simulated model. They do not establish that live flies optimize the same objective. The comparison selected among 20 objectives and seven candidate internal representations; decoder hyperparameters were tuned on the biological data. Agreement is not an untouched validation of a uniquely identified biological objective.
evidence.ai_role: DIAYN and other learned intrinsic-motivation algorithms train hierarchical policies. Fitted elastic-net decoders compare future-turn information in the models and prior fly recordings.
